The CLARITY Act heads to Senate Banking Committee markup tomorrow. Let’s secure America's position as the global innovation leader & Crypto Capital of the World! 🇺🇸 https://t.co/BG2VSxt1GH

I appreciate the president's intent of ensuring that local communities have economic development opportunities, but this is a local government decision. [...] Local governments need to consider the potential harms or impacts through electricity rates, through water, through other impacts and way those against possible benefits like additional tax base and good-paying jobs. But these are ultimately decisions of local communities.

Those are some of the important guardrails that have to happen, as well as hiring local jobs and just being sure that there are no impacts on the community – but then communities can make their own decision. There's going to be positive tax base opportunities here for communities, as well as good-paying jobs.
As a senator, I'd have the obligation to be sure that we get the benefits of innovation, without having any harm from a new technology.

When we talk about AI around the state, I always am talking about data centers. And let me be clear, I will always protect Montana. We need to be sure that if a data center company comes into this state, that they're transparent, they're clear about their cost to the community and other effects. We also have to have clear guardrails set. Any data center company needs to pay its own way, and they need to create local jobs.

They also need to be sure that they have no adverse water effects, not on water users or on water quality. They also need to guarantee that there'll be no electricity increases on Montana families. In fact, they should help lower electricity rates.

And even if those guardrails are met, data center companies need to work with local communities to get their acceptance. So as Senator, I'll work to be sure that we have transparency, we have clear guardrails, and that Montana communities are heard.
As United States Attorney, I also saw firsthand how China was trying to get to technological parity through intellectual property theft. We need to put a stop to that.

They need to make sure they pay their own way and they need to hire local jobs, they also need to protect our water, we can't have adverse impacts on water quality or on other water users. We should leave this to our local communities to decide.
